2026 SEMA Show • Nissan Seeks Adventures at 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas With Frontier, Pathfinder, Armada Concepts
Two Special Hot Wheels for November of 2026 That Won’t Come Easy or Cheap
20 photos
Photo: Mattel
With every Hot Wheels story I write, I try to pass on some of the knowledge I’ve learned in 10+ years of being part of the hobby. Some of the information can easily work for other hobbies as well. Don’t build a collection with the sole purpose of trying to impress other people!
Buy the cars you truly love: it doesn’t matter if they’re just Mainline collectibles as long as you’re happy. To me, upgrading to the Premium lines has been an improvement, but that hasn’t stopped me from occasionally buying basic entry items from both Hot Wheels and Matchbox. And while I’ve had over a dozen Red Line Club models at home at one point, I only own half of them right now.
And I only intend to hold on to the Porsche 959 for as long as possible. Older RLCs are often easier to get, as the hype almost always goes away and prices suddenly start to drop. So if you like the idea of adding one of the new RLC releases to your collection but can’t buy it directly from Mattel, just put in on hold for one to two years until the right offer pops up.
It won’t be as easy with Convention-special items, as those are typically the only ones with a limited production run these days. There are exceptions, and the '72 Stingray Convertible (4,000 units) that was the dinner car at the 40th Annual Hot Wheels Collectors Convention in Los Angeles can cost as little as $75 on eBay.
Meanwhile, you’re better off not looking at the prices for the 2022 Porsche 911 GT3 RS (6,200 units), as that was a highly-desirable casting from the get-go. Why am I telling you all this? Well, the Mexico Hot Wheels Convention is coming right up, and you can buy a Mariachi-themed version of Brendon Vetuskey’s Chevrolet C10 if you’ll be attending the show.
I think it will cost around $100 on the spot, which means it could easily find its way onto eBay for over $200. We’ll have to wait a few days to find out. I can tell you that going after Vetuskey’s new Hot Wheels RLC Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 should be a lot easier. His older '18 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon casting has had a good time with two Super Treasure Hunt iterations, one NFT Garage release and multiple Premium models.
But it didn’t have an opening hood and a nicely detailed Hellephant V8 engine. That’s right, you’ve heard me say it: Mattel has finally manage to improve the way the engine bay looks like on its RLC models, although I suspect a direct comparison to Pop Race or Kaido House will still lead to the same result as it did before. Spectraflame Pink isn’t my first choice of color for a vehicle like this, but I can live with it this time.
Having brand new wheels is an extra bonus at this point, and you’ll need a peak under the parachute to see the “SHE DVL” plate. The Demon 170 goes live on Mattel Creations on November 10, 2026 at 9 AM PT for $28. The limit of two units per customer still stands, and I think there’s a good chance you can buy this item if you try to do so within the first hour. If you won’t be able to score one, eBay listings for it are still in a relatively decent spot for now.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Toyota Crown Signia Gets GT-S Concept Treatment for SEMA, Becomes a Sleek Wagon
Fanatec Gran Turismo Eifel Cup 2026 Has Started and You Can Win Real Prizes
29 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I just recently received my copy of the Mäder Morse Field Recordings Porsche 964 Carrera RS Book. To me, it looks like a love letter to Zuffenhausen’s super-lightweight, RWD-only 911 from the early ‘90s. I’m talking about 442 pages of valuable information and photos on the 964 Carrera RS family.
Its author is Christoph Mäder, and he needed three and a half years of research to create this book. I’ve barely had time to have a quick look at it so far, and I just want to lock myself up in a room for a few days and get the job done.
I will be interviewing Christoph shortly to learn more about the process behind creating this Porsche -infused masterpiece, and you can bet I developed a serious appetite to somehow get closer to the 964 RS as soon as possible.
While I know quite a few 911 Turbo and 911 GT3 RS owners, the same doesn’t apply to the 964 RS. So realistically speaking, my only option was to head on over to Gran Turismo 7. As luck would have it, Polyphony partnered up with Fanatec for a global Time Trial event around the Nurburgring GP layout.
We’ll be driving a replica of the Black Falcon Team Fanatec Porsche 911 GT3 R, and I knew the 964 RS would serve as a great practice car ahead of the main event.
Practice Session 1 Photo: autoevolution I did not have one in my garage, but it just so happened to be available at the Used Car Dealership. Seeing it in Speed Yellow was even better for me as that’s one of my favorite colors for the 911. I paid 211,000 credits for the car, which is more than half a million credits cheaper than the 911 Carrera RS (901) '73.
What really shocked me was that the price for the 911 GT1 Strassenversion has gone up to 18 million credits, when I clearly remember it being just 10 million a few months ago. Anyway, the 964 RS in GT7 features the 3,6-liter engine which has a maximum output of 255 bhp, with the whole car weighing 2,712 lbs (1,230 kg).
I knew it would by no means get close to a two-minute lap at the GP layout, but it was bound to be fun regardless. I was already up at 124 mph (200 kph) before Turn 1, and found myself going sideways on multiple occasions through the tighter turns.
It’s a reminder that you don’t need 1,000 hp to enjoy driving, and it took me two minutes and 28 seconds for the full lap. That’s three seconds faster than my result in the MAZDA SPIRIT RACING ROADSTER 12R '25 which joined GT7 in Update 1.63.
Nurburgring GP Time Trial Photo: autoevolution I didn’t realize this new event started on the second of November. That’s because I typically only use my PS5 on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays. I’d love it if more Time Trials had us driving replicas of modern racecars such as this Porsche 911 GT3 R, even though we’re all free to choose the liveries we want. Over 80,000 players have posted a fast lap so far, and it didn’t surprise me to see guys like K.Drumont and D.Chafe on top of the leaderboard.
I assume only a handful of people might be able to get a 1:56.xxx fast lap like they did. The event is split in three regions: Asia-Oceania, the Americas, and Europe-Middle East-Africa. The top player from each region will be able to choose between a Fanatec Gran Turismo DD Pro (8Nm) steering wheel or a Fanatec Podium Pedals Sport pedal set.
Given how much Fanatec has grown over the years, wouldn’t it be nice if it threw in a few awards for random participants, too? Anyway, we can still chase after the Gold, Silver and Bronze Record rewards and the credits included in the package. The target for Gold currently stands at just over two minutes, while Bronze is at 2:08.635.
BoP rules apply here, which is why the 911 GT3 R will go from 557 bhp to just 451, also gaining 196 lbs/89 kgs in the process. I was too eager on my first two laps, which is how I ended up in the grass. I’m still struggling with the first section on this layout, especially since you can hit 147 mph/237 kph before Turn 1. I was quite close to a Silver finish on my third attempt (2:03.201), and I should pay attention to Tidgney’s tutorial (included at the bottom) to improve a bit.
Practice Session 2 Photo: autoevolution I mentioned the 911 GT1 Strassenversion because I knew I wanted two “new” cars for my practice session at the other Time Trial available in GT7. This event at Fuji International Speedway went live on Thursday, November 5th, and it’s all about GT3 machines.
That means we once again have the privilege of choosing between 53 different cars without having to pay any credits to enjoy them for two weeks. Luckily me, I unlocked a McLaren P1 GTR from a 5-Star Roulette Ticket (Seasonal Menu), and I figured I might as well drive it for a few days.
With over 900 bhp on tap, it’s no surprise it can hit 195 mph/315 kph before Turn 1 at Fuji. I knew this would be my fastest session of the day at the Japanese track, even though I was constantly struggling to use all of the car’s power.
I ultimately needed one minute and 38 seconds for the first lap, which is one second slower than my best result in the tuned 911 GT1, and seven second slower than what I could accomplish with the F1500T-A. The latter only weighs a fraction of what the P1 GTR does, and it’s also cheaper, too!
Practice Session 3 Photo: autoevolution I don’t even recall where the 6-Star Roulette ticket came from today, and also didn’t mind unlocking the NISSAN CONCEPT 2020 Vision Gran Turismo from it. This one-million credits machine feels and sounds pretty much like an R35 GT-R on steroids: can you believe it’s over a decade old already?
It comes standard on Sports Medium tires, and I didn’t want to deal with that sort of problem when the twin-turbo hybrid V6 inside has an output of about 700 bhp.
I went from start to finish in 105 seconds on my first attempt, before realizing I hadn’t even used the “Overtake” button. I improved by almost three seconds on the next lap, struggling with understeer through the faster corners.
I guess that if any of the guys at the top could have driven this instead of the GT3 machines, they could have only needed about 95 seconds for the full lap.
Fuji International Speedway Time Trial Photo: autoevolution I always get nostalgic seeing the Skyline Super Silhouette ‘84 as an option for these events, but you can hardly expect to get close to the Gold Record Reward in one of these (that’s my take since I’m slow). Some of the GT500 and Super GT cars of old are on the menu as well, and today I went for a mix of three European cars and two Japanese ones.
I started with the Ferrari 296 GT3, which loses 150 bhp and gains 176 lbs/80 kg after the BoP comes into play. You can expect a top speed of around 161 mph/260 kph before Turn 1! I needed one minute and 46 seconds for my first lap, still struggling to find the right approach. Switching to the 458 Italia GT3 might not seem like the best idea, but it’s easier to start accelerating earlier through a corner as there’s no boost involved.
I get along well with this 10-year-old car, which is how I easily improved by almost 2.5 seconds on my first attempt. The Mazda RX Vision GT3 evo has less power to rely on than both of the two Ferraris, but it’s also a bit lighter. It reached the highest top speed for me today (262 kph), which also helped me “find” 0.133 seconds along the way.
I didn’t enjoy the Lexus RC F GT3 as much, especially since the McLaren F1 GTR came next. I went for a simple white on white look, enjoying the lightest setup of the day while losing my turbocharger in the process. It was my best result of the session: 1:43.644! If you can’t afford paying 20 million credits for one, drive the hell out of it until the 19th of November and thank me later!

source_document.body:
2026 SEMA Show • SRT Performance Joins the 2026 SEMA Show Featuring the First-Ever Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept
Owner Pulls 1968 Ford Mustang From Storage Unit, Decides To Sell. Worth $6K?
45 photos
Photo: eBay seller fjdeals
Mustangs make for fantastic daily drivers, and this 1968 specimen is here with this one goal in mind. The car looks like it’s been sitting for a long time in a storage unit, so the reason it landed on eBay has everything to do with its long-term objective.
It must find a new home, get a complete restoration, and eventually return to the road without eating up many dollars.
Is this even possible, in the first place? It is, especially because this Mustang still has an engine under the hood. Is it worth it? This depends on many factors, and I recommend that every potential buyer call the seller and ask for a digital walkaround before making an offer.
Photo: eBay seller fjdeals The 1968 Mustang production fell, but it wasn’t necessarily the fault of Ford’s superstar. The 60-day strike that took place in September and November impacted the Mustang output, so eventually, Ford ended the year with only 317,148 units shipped to American buyers.
On paper, the decline looks significant, especially considering the 472,121 units shipped in 1967. The good news was that the hardtop continued to dominate sales with nearly 250K cars, while the fastback was also popular - though not even close to the hardtop - with 42,325 units
There’s a good reason why the hardtop was so popular. It was the most affordable version in the entire lineup, starting at $2,602, whereas the convertible was significantly more expensive, with the base configuration priced at $2,814.
But for this money, you only got a 200 six, and it’s no secret that many people today would rather turn their backs and walk away. However, the six was an honest choice for someone who just wanted the Mustang for typical daily drives to the supermarket and picking up the kids from school.
Ford obviously offered significantly more powerful upgrades, and the top choice was based on the 427, this time rated at 390 horsepower. It was an expensive upgrade, as it could be had for $622. Unsurprisingly, this was a very rarely ordered engine, so if you somehow come across such a specimen that has the W code in the VIN, you’d better not miss the opportunity to get it.
Photo: eBay seller fjdeals This Mustang isn’t fitted with this super-desirable engine and is somehow at the opposite pole. It has a six under the hood, and while I’m pretty sure that collectors are ready to walk away at this point, I think this specimen makes for a great candidate for a father-son project or a simple restoration to build a daily driver.
The six is still in good shape, according to the seller. It starts and runs, but you really shouldn't consider this car a roadworthy vehicle. The owner says that it needs work, and the transmission requires particular attention before the Mustang can go on a long trip.
Photo: eBay seller fjdeals As for the overall condition of the Mustang, you don’t need to be a die-hard restoration guy to anticipate that most of the work will go to the underside. There’s rust on the floors, and my recommendation is that you raise the car on a lift to see everything with your eyes.
On the plus side, patching a Mustang or installing new floors really isn’t that hard, and finding new sheets of metal is quite easy. There are lots of donors out there, and if you’re lucky, you might be able to find a full car without an engine for only a couple of thousand dollars.
If you’re here because you’re in the market for an original Mustang, this specimen could end up disappointing you for obvious reasons. There’s a new stereo in the car, and the closer you look, the more aftermarket things you’ll notice, so that’s why I believe that an in-person inspection would come in so handy.
Photo: eBay seller fjdeals Overall, this Mustang doesn’t look all that bad, and I would really be interested in finding out more about what happened in the past and the previous ownership. This Mustang looks to be parked in a storage unit, so I would love to know how it ended up there and how many years it spent away from the road.
As for the price, it goes without saying that such a Mustang can’t be expensive. It has a six, it’s been sitting for a while, and requires a complete restoration or, at least, urgent work to return to the road.
The seller believes that $5,900 is a fair price, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, therefore suggesting that other offers would also be considered if someone is committed to buying this car.
The vehicle is parked in Baltimore, Maryland, and if you buy the car in its current condition, you’ll also need to look into shipping costs from the storage unit to your garage.
Via // eBay

source_document.body:
2026 SEMA Show • Stellantis Uses Direct Connection to Unleash No Less Than Six New HEMI V8 Crate Engine Packages
How Much Is a New Mansory-Tuned Audi RS Q8?
14 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Audi’s Q8 blew eight candles off its birthday cake earlier this year, and that makes it old in today’s automotive game. This is why some might think that production of this model ended, but that’s not the case, because it is still being put together at the Bratislava factory in Slovakia.
By the way, it’s not the only model based on the Volkswagen Group’s old MLB Evo platform to still be around, as this also applies to the Lamborghini Urus, third-gen Porsche Cayenne, and Bentley Bentayga, and the latter is even older, as assembly commenced back in 2015. The previous Audi Q7, Q8, and A6, the demised VW Touareg, and other vehicles also utilized this construction.
Everyone and their pet knows that the Audi Q8 takes on the likes of the BMW X6 and Mercedes GLE Coupe, whereas its range-topping version, the RS Q8, is a rival to the likes of the X6 M and GLE 63 Coupe. The RS Q8 was unveiled at the Los Angeles Auto Show back in 2019, sharing its V8 lump with the era’s RS 6 and RS 7. Like the lesser SQ8 , it has a ZF eight-speed automatic transmission, and quattro all-wheel drive.
We will delve a bit more into the oily bits in just a few moments, but first, let’s put the spotlight on the example pictured in the gallery, which has been tuned by Mansory, and is now looking for a new home in the United States of America. This Audi RS Q8 is a 2026 model year car, and it has only 644 miles (1,036 km) under its belt. Therefore, you are looking at a brand-new machine, and it can be yours, if you have deep pockets and want it.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Care to talk about the novelties? Well, these include stuff such as the add-ons in the front bumper, including the new apron with blades on the sides, the extra daytime running lights below the side vents, and the vented hood, among other things. The wheel arches are now on the muscular side of things, so this Audi RS Q8 is now wider than the stock one. There are also new side skirt attachments on deck, as we can see from these pictures.
The images also reveal the back end of this premium mid-size super crossover coupe, which features an entirely new diffuser. The latter element has a five-slat diffuser that is very aggressive. The tailpipes are no longer the OEM ones, as the dual oval exhaust tips have been replaced by new ones. The vehicle has a matte black look on the outside, some glossy black elements, some dry carbon accents, and even forged carbon elements.
The wheels are also new, and they are not oversized. They spin around the red brake calipers, and these are the things that provide the most contrast on the outside. Step inside and you will see bright orange leather upholstery on the seats, on the lower parts of the dashboard, and on the central section of the steering wheel. The cockpit also features some Alcantara elements, as well as red stitching, and some carbon fiber trim, among other things.
Elsewhere, this modded Audi RS Q8 has a digital gauge cluster, an infotainment system in the middle of the dashboard, and a third display to control the HVAC system. There is also a large panoramic sunroof, and the images shared in the gallery reveal other things that one would expect from such a thing.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Weirdly, the vendor, which is known as @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, hasn’t mentioned the oily bits at all. And while that would normally mean that the powertrain hasn’t been modded, this is Mansory that we are talking about, so we are not entirely certain that the assembly retains its stock output and thrust.
If it is stock, then you are looking at 631 bhp (640 ps/571 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque. A bone stock Audi RS Q8 takes just 3.4 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and that makes it roughly two-tenths of a second slower than the new Lamborghini Urus SE Performante, which has 801 hp (812 ps/598 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque combined from its plug-in hybrid V8.
Now, we have told you everything that we know about the pictured Audi RS Q8 with Mansory goodies save for the asking price. So, how much do you think you have to pay if you want to buy it? That would be $269,995. By comparison, a brand-new Audi RS Q8 performance from the 2027 model year will set you back a minimum of $139,700, which is the official MSRP in the United States of America.
Is this tuned example worth more than $100K more? You be the judge of that, and feel free to tell us what you think about it in the comments area below. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)

2026 SEMA Show • Stellantis Uses Direct Connection to Unleash No Less Than Six New HEMI V8 Crate Engine Packages
2027 Hot Wheels Boulevard Mix 3 Preview: We're Getting Two New Cars!
25 photos
Photo: Lamley Group
You may have noticed that motorcycle manufacturers have been unveiling a lot of novelties at the EICMA show this year. One particular brand just launched a superbike that has been completely under wraps for some time now. The funny thing is that I’ve known about it for four years now.
It’s a company that I’m not particularly into, which is why you don’t see me reviewing any of its products. It has been growing like crazy over the past few years, and I was certain they hadn’t abandoned the project. I just didn’t expect it would take so long to arrive. Anyway, I’m not here to talk about bikes, but there is something in that first paragraph that you could use to talk about Hot Wheels collectibles as well.
Just think of all the previews we’re getting after the Convention in Los Angeles. These new models didn’t pop up out of thin air. I don’t know exactly how much time they spend in development, but it’s probably safe to assume we’re talking about at least 12 months. So, looking at the next Boulevard collectibles, the team in charge of the project has likely been aware of what’s coming since 2025.
That has to be both fun and grueling at the same time, as each one of the designers likely signed an NDA since the day they started working for the company. This new video from Los Angeles gives us a better look at the first two Boulevard mixes for next year, so that could be exciting if you haven’t seen them so far.
I’m starting to think that I should pre-order Mix 2 if I genuinely want to have my first premium iteration of Ronald Wong’s BNR34. It looks stunning in Millennium Jade, and it would be my first Hot Wheels model with the SPLIT6 Real Riders wheels. Right now I’d like to focus on our first look at Mix 3, which is missing a car.
Photo: Lamley Group The 2005 Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution IX Wagon is back for its second iteration, and this time we can enjoy it without having to buy a secondary item like we did with the Car Culture 2-Pack release. The Greddy livery is certainly an upgrade, and somehow having paint on the 6-Spoke Real Riders makes them look much better than ever before.
I think it’s been a while since we last saw a Greddy-themed model, and I’m sure this will go nicely with the Sakura Sprinter and Nissan Laurel 2000 SGX from the first-ever Team Transport mix or the Porsche 962 from the 2017 Car Culture: Race Day set to name a few of the options. I’m sure people could start enjoying Greddy models just as much as they do HKS ones if Mattel focused on the topic for a bit.
You’ll never hear me raving about a modern Mercedes-Benz vehicle, which is why even I am surprised to see how hard I’ve fallen for the '72 Mercedes-Benz 280 SEL 4.5 . It feels like an automotive masterpiece, and Mark Jones has done an amazing done at creating this casting. We haven’t had a new iteration since the 2022 Car Culture: Autostrasse set which I recently unboxed and took photos of.
The 2021 2-pack version isn’t quite as nice as it’s on the wrong wheels and features a boring color. Meanwhile, the First Edition (2020 Modern Classics) is epic in Metalflake Dark Blue. I want to be excited about the 2027 variation, but the gold finish reminds me of the 2026 Chase drama and I don’t want to be a part of any of that. It might be easy to lose track of how many Chevy C10 castings Mattel has come up with over the years, especially if it’s not something you’d normally pay attention to.
Photo: Lamley Group The new casting is a 1974 model, and I’d buy it right away if it showed up with the black finish and the blue interior. Seeing Kristina’s photos points to a different kind of direction, but I was still excited to hear the word “rusty” mid-conversation. I still have the 1967 Chevy Custom C-10 that Rob Matthes designed, and it wasn’t that long ago that I unboxed Ryu Asada’s '67 Chevy C10 as well.
Brendon Vetuskey created the '69 Chevy C-10 which is an RLC exclusive release (and might show up at an event in Mexico soon), and he was also in charge of this Premium C10 from the preview video. The Chevy is one of two new castings inside, as a new Subaru Impreza WRX STI is on its way for 2027.
It’s a replica of the Hawkeye that closed an entire chapter for this car, as Subaru switched to a hatchback right after it. This new casting arrives just after the Subaru Impreza Rally RC car, and two other Impreza releases in 2026 alone! Meanwhile, Mattel is using a 10-year old casting for the Racing Culture series, and I assume it’s all a matter of timing. Do you think the team in El Segundo is going to risk not releasing this new model in a Subaru standard blue paintjob?

Amazon isn’t just electrifying its American delivery operations. The virtual big box stores that Bezos built understands the benefits of EVs as well as anyone, and they’re working hard to deploy electric vehicles everywhere they can . And now, that global push is extending to India.
Indian automaker TATA Motors has announced a deal with Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India . When it goes live, it will be the largest electric truck deployment by in India and mark Amazon’s most significant move to extend its Indian fleet electrification beyond last-mile logistics.
“India is accelerating towards electric mobility and the realization of Viksit Bharat 2047,” says Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy, Hon’ble Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Government of India. “The collaboration between TATA Motors and Amazon shows what that looks like in practice: sustained demand from a nationwide logistics network met by electric trucks manufactured in India. Through PM E-DRIVE, the Government will continue to support this transition, and I look forward to more such efforts in powering green logistics.”
Good deal
TATA executives at project launch; via Amazon.
In addition to being a big deal for TATA, the 3,000 electric truck deal represents a serous bump to India’s deployed electric truck fleet, and are a major step towards the wide-scale electrification of freight transportation across the country – that’s not just good for Amazon’s fuel bills, it’s good for everyone and everything that breathes air, too.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
“ Electrifying our logistics and transportation network is an important part of Amazon’s goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040 ,” says Abhinav Singh, Vice President, Operations, Amazon, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkey. “We have made significant progress in India, with more than 15,000 electric vehicles operating across 500-plus cities . To enable this transition, we are also supporting the development of infrastructure and solutions that make EV adoption easier for our carrier partners and drivers. We are now setting a bold vision to scale electric trucking , addressing one of the toughest challenges in decarbonizing transportation. Our collaboration with TATA Motors marks an important step towards realizing this vision. By combining our strengths, we aim to accelerate the deployment of electric trucks across more routes, starting with intracity operations and expanding to India’s major freight corridors.”
The truck, itself
TATA truck deal, via Amazon.
The truck Amazon will be deploying in these record numbers is a version of the Tata Ultra E.7, a 7.5-tonne (~16,000 lb.) straight truck powered by a 240 kW (~320 hp) electric motor drawing power from a 96 kWh LFP battery pack. The truck’s makers claim a loaded range of up to 130 km (~80 miles) on a single charge, with DC fast-charging that’s capable enough to keep the trucks charged up between deliveries.
Amazon’s new TATA electric delivery trucks will support the transport of goods between warehouse facilities – which means traveling across cities and along India’s national freight corridors.

2026 SEMA Show • Nissan Seeks Adventures at 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas With Frontier, Pathfinder, Armada Concepts
Mitsubishi Lancer Comes Back to Digital Life Thanks to the Nissan Sentra, Do You Like It For the US?
10 photos
Photo: Theottle / YouTube
The Japanese automaker is working hard to exit the shadow cone it put itself into a while back, and not just in North America where the roster is now composed of three variations of the Outlander, an expensive fastback EV, and the quirky Eclipse Cross.
For example, the reborn Mitsubishi Pajero is both winning back old customers and attracting new ones from other brands, but also keeping the spirit of the Lancer alive in a crossover produced by Foxtron Vehicle Technologies, while North America is suffering.
We heard that the pre-orders for the Mitsubishi Pajero are going just fine, and also in Australia, Foxtron, the automotive arm of Taiwanese electronics giant Foxconn, is making the Mitsubishi ASX VR-e for the company based on their Foxtron Bria model. Designed by Pininfarina, the CUV aims to keep the Lancer EVO spirit alive, with the flagship ASX VR-e GSR packing 459 hp and 700 Nm (516 lb-ft) of torque!
But what about North America? Well, the Mitsubishi Montero is left dwindling across the rumor mill without any official confirmation of its return to the US market, and instead Mitsubishi is going to the 2026 SEMA Show with an adventurous Outlander – the Diamond Trail Edition . It’s made for the dirt and even got riddled with additional accessories, but it’s still the same riff off an old song, right?
No worries, as some folks have solutions – and they might be much better than taking the Nissan Leaf, rebadging it as a Mitsubishi (Eclipse Sportback EV), and selling it way more expensive (+$8k) than the base donor vehicle. Mitsubishi is going to turn the cards around by making for Honda a Triton-based mid-size body-on-frame pickup truck.
Anyway, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to provide an alternative. This virtual artist, better known as " Theottle " on social media, has resorted to CGI slicing and dicing the Nissan Sentra to imagine a reborn Mitsubishi Lancer, including for North America, in his latest behind-the-scenes making-of video.
He muses that “Mitsubishi and Nissan have long shared platforms, technologies, and vehicle development programs. In recent years, several Mitsubishi models have been based on Nissan products, including the Eclipse hatchback EV and an upcoming pickup truck for the North American market. This raises an interesting question: could Mitsubishi consider reviving the Lancer using the Nissan Sentra as a foundation?”
So, he took the all-new Nissan Sentra and combined “Sentra's underlying structure with body panels inspired by the Opel Astra, whose proportions and surfacing I believe closely resemble those of recent Mitsubishi models.” Everything was then reinterpreted for the possibility of creating a modern Mitsubishi Lancer based on the latest Nissan Sentra (B19), featuring “a distinct Mitsubishi identity.”
As such, the “front and rear feature headlights and taillights inspired by the Mitsubishi Destinator and the new Pajero, and the result is a contemporary interpretation of the Lancer that blends Nissan engineering with Mitsubishi styling cues.” Cool or not?

Hyundai Recalls Kona Electric and Veloster N for Airbag Software Concern
24 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Believe it or not, Hyundai spent more than two years investigating a problem that can leave two very different vehicles without functioning airbags. The root cause behind this condition? According to Hyundai, corrupted data inside the airbag control unit. The subsequent recall covers 37,901 examples of the Kona Electric and the Veloster N, and that's only in the US market.
In this part of the world, no fewer than 331 unique reports alleging the condition have been received by the South Korean manufacturer since October 2019. None involved an injury, and that sure is fortunate considering the failure can disable the seatbelt pretensioners as well.
The recall population splits between 29,058 examples of the 2019 through 2023 model year Kona Electric and 8,843 units of the 2019 through 2022 model year Veloster N. And yes, I'm missing the quirky Veloster N as much as the next guy. The common denominator here is the airbag control software. More to the point, a reboot at the wrong moment disables the airbags.
The subject control unit monitors crash signals, commanding the deployment of the airbags and seatbelt pretensioners. Obviously enough, a pretensioner is designed to tighten the belt during a collision, keeping the occupant in the right position before the airbags do their job.
Hyundai determined that airbag control unit data can become corrupted while said unit writes information to its internal memory. A reboot or interruption in electrical power during the writing operation leaves the controller with corrupted data, compromising the system.
Photo: Hyundai Motor Company The compromised state becomes evident once the airbag malfunction indicator illuminates. Hyundai filed this recall with the NHTSA as campaign 26V728, but the automaker calls it 311. Sadly, I cannot guarantee that anyone in charge of safety at Hyundai Motor America loves 311 the band.
Anyway, the ACU responds by deactivating the airbag system, leaving the occupants without the expected restraint protection in the event of a crash that calls for the deployment of the airbags and pretensioners. ZF Group is listed in the recall documentation as the supplier of the ACU, which features no fewer than three distinct part numbers in Hyundai's parts system.
HMA's North America Safety Office started looking into this matter on August 19, 2024, after identifying an increasing number of warranty claims involving the airbag warning light. Five ACUs were recovered that year for examination. Hyundai and ZF worked together, but finding a reproducible fault took an excruciatingly long time.
Electrical tests were conducted between May 2025 and August 2025, followed by vehicle-level replication tests between September 2025 and August 2026. Ultimately, the mad lads did it, confirming the root cause and becoming aware of the safety risks posed by this issue.
Dealers are to update all suspect vehicles, albeit only with the specialized service tool via the OBD-II port. There is no over-the-air option available. Customers will be formally notified in January 2027. In the meantime, the NHTSA's VIN lookup system can already recognize the affected vehicles.

2026 SEMA Show • Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
1968 Shelby GT500 Ragtop 4-Speed Sat 26 Years Untouched, Car Nut Finds It in Pieces, It's a 1-of-9
68 photos
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins
"I don't know how you turn down a red 4-speed convertible." Let’s get things straight, this isn’t a Camry Solara we’re talking here, but one of the greatest Detroit icons ever: a 1968 Shelby Mustang GT500. Ragtop. With a 4-speed. Granted, it’s in boxes, but everything’s there. Even grown men can’t resist the urge for a full-sized LEGO, given the opportunity. Dennis Collins approves; he just rescued the car.
The Texas-based collector and restorer flew to Punta Gorda, Florida, to meet Garry Gilbert, an award-winning Ford craftsman whose immaculate workshop also houses a stunning 1962 Ford Galaxie 500 finished in a deep Dodge Hellcat burgundy shade. Gilbert has laid out the disassembled Shelby like an indoor swap meet, with folding tables stacked high with trim, date-coded seat belts, restored components, and boxes of spare 428 Cobra Jet engine parts neatly organized for inspection.
The car actually belongs to a longtime friend of Gilbert from Indiana, who purchased the drop-top at the Mecum Indianapolis auction in the fall of 2023, with a hammer price of $72,000 (final price $79,200, after fees). Already owning several collector vehicles, the buyer simply wanted a worry-free classic driver he could take to the grocery store without fretting over a stray door ding. Having relied on Gilbert for mechanical work back in Indiana, he shipped the Shelby south for a basic service.
Once Gilbert put the convertible on his neighbor's lift next door, however, that simple plan evaporated. A closer inspection underneath revealed that the aging pony car needed far more than fresh brakes and a fuel system flush. After discussing the options, the owner told Gilbert to pull the engine and transmission, go through the drivetrain mechanically, and find a metal specialist to install new floors so the car would be safe.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins That decision launched a cross-country odyssey that saw the Shelby spend more time on trailers than on the asphalt. The convertible traveled north to a body shop in Pennsylvania, where the craftsman braced the open-top unibody and welded in a complete floor pan, torque boxes, frame rails, and a fresh trunk floor before back injuries halted his progress. Gilbert eventually hauled the shell back to Florida to find another painter.
Hoping for the same high standard of work that graced his Galaxie 500, Gilbert delivered the Shelby to a local Florida shop. Instead, the convertible fell victim to the dreaded body shop jail, sitting untouched in a corner while months slipped away. Growing restless back in Indiana, the owner finally decided to wash his hands of the stalled project and asked Gilbert to find a buyer who could finish it.
For a seasoned Shelby specialist like Collins, the pedigree of this 1968 convertible makes it almost impossible to ignore. Bearing Shelby serial number 8T03S116056-00244, it is an early production car, confirmed by the single courtesy-light button in the driver's door jamb denoting a non-tilt-away steering column. Out of 4,450 Shelbys built for 1968, only around 400 were GT500 convertibles, and just 150 left the factory with a 4-speed manual gearbox.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Digging into the paperwork compiled with the help of Florida marque expert Brian Styles and a Deluxe Marti Report, the rarity of car 244 gets even better. While most buyers who ordered code T Candyapple Red paint with a code 6A black luxury bucket seat interior selected a white folding roof, this convertible was specified with a black power top, no LeMans stripes, no air conditioning, and rare roll-bar surfboard brackets.
According to the factory production breakdown, that exact combination of colors and equipment makes this GT500 convertible 1 of only 9 examples ever produced. Better still, the car retains its original Shelby American serial plate, its Ford door data tag, and a surviving corner of its metal buck tag. With 78,000 miles (some 125,529 kilometers), showing on the odometer, the car's mechanical history proved just as fascinating as its statistics.
Sitting on a rolling stand in Gilbert's garage is the car's original, numbers-matching 428 Police Interceptor V8 block, which had never been removed from the engine bay prior to this teardown. Historical records from Jack Loftus Ford in Hinsdale, Illinois, showed the Shelby had been brought in under warranty early in its life for engine noise, prompting dealer technicians to free a valve and replace the right cylinder head.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins When Gilbert pulled the intake manifold off to inspect the short block, he discovered that the dealership mechanics had never bothered to remove the valley pan heat shield. Lifting that metal tray for the first time in 58 years, Gilbert found a snapped pushrod lying quietly inside the lifter valley, a clear souvenir from an early driver who likely missed a shift between 2nd and 3rd gear and over-revved the big-block.
Fortunately, the cylinder walls still displayed their factory hone crosshatching, allowing Gilbert to preserve the original short block while rebuilding both heads with new valves, springs, and fuel guides. He plugged the ports from the seized California smog pump, bolted on a restored 1969 carburetor built by Air Fuel Spark, resealed the original 4-speed transmission, rebuilt the 3.50:1 rear axle, and had the original C8 radiator recored.
The best surprise arrives when Collins dropped to his knees beside the folding tables to inspect the original bucket seats. Reaching into the rusted springs, he pulls out a crumpled wad of paper that Gilbert had dismissed as an old napkin. Carefully unfolding the fragile document, Collins reveals a large, legible section of the original factory build sheet confirming the T paint, 6A interior, 29 black top, and 3.50 axle code.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Although the Texas car hunter admits he originally hoped for a three-month turnaround rather than a one-year bodywork marathon to replace the rear quarters and source the original wheels and hubcaps from Indiana, the newly discovered build sheet seals the deal. Shaking Gilbert's hand, Collins talks himself into taking over the project, bolts the rear seat and console into the primed cabin for safekeeping, and rolls the Shelby out into the Florida rain.
With all four of his own transport rigs and drivers busy on other hauls, Collins enlists a trusted contract hauler to load the convertible, its freshly painted 428 V8, and its 4-speed gearbox for the trip back to Wylie, Texas.

2026 SEMA Show • This Batmobile-Looking Lamborghini Temerario Is on Display at SEMA
The Chrysler Sebring Coupe Returns to Life With Pacifica DNA, Though Only Across Imagination Land
11 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
Everyone has been pretty busy over the past week across the automotive industry in North America, including Stellantis . They balanced the recently concluded 2026 SEMA Show and other things, but not revivals – at least not of the passenger car variety.
Stellantis did feature a reborn nameplate – the SRT Performance division worked for the first time on a Jeep concept, the Wrangler Scrambler Concept , reimagining the legendary Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler with modern flair. But other than that, they were preoccupied by The Brotherhood of Muscle returning to NASCAR Cup Racing, as Dodge is returning to NASCAR Cup Series racing alongside Ram Trucks and Kaulig Racing, which now serves as the two brands’ anchor team.
What about Chrysler ? Well, the ailing brand hasn’t made the news rounds in an official capacity since August, when Chrysler debuted two custom Pacifica concepts at Roadkill Nights Powered by Dodge in Pontiac, Michigan, on August 8, and only the rumor mill has taken care of it since then. According to the latest reports, the brand will soon become a multi-vehicle marque again with the introduction of the Airflow and the Arrow and Arrow Cross beneath it – giving budget-conscious buyers additional CUV options on the market.
But what about passenger cars? Well, it seems that Pacifica is destined to rule alone from the minivan category, as the three new entries will swell the ranks of crossover SUVs. Not across Imagination Land, though, if this member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI has anything to say.
Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Chrysler car – the return of the Chrysler Sebring mid-size nameplate in coupe format.
The original Chrysler Sebring was produced from 1995 to 2010 in convertible and sedan or coupe body styles, with the two coupe generations created with help from Mitsubishi and produced at the Japanese automaker’s Normal, Illinois facility. Now the unofficial, hypothetical design project imagines the resurrection of the Chrysler Sebring as an affordable mid-size coupe with classic proportions and Chrysler Pacifica’s new visual identity embedded at the front.
Reception from the fans has been mostly positive, and people are saying that “it’s a nice-looking car” and that the Mitsubishi Eclipse Coupe should be coming back, too. Someone also asked for the convertible version to bring back the LeBaron moniker, by the way. That’s all fine and dandy, but what should power this good-looking coupe?
Chrysler could easily borrow the STLA Medium architecture from within the Stellantis ranks and perhaps the standard output version of the 3.0-liter Hurricane inline-six. It could be detuned to around 300 hp with a lot of low-rpm torque grunt in order to keep it affordable and out of Dodge Charger’s way. So, what do you think?
